findings: High: `choose_figure()` in [scripts/build_input_representation_atlas.py](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/scripts/build_input_representation_atlas.py:204) ranks whole figures by model-name text overlap, route citations, and generic words like `architecture/workflow`, but it never inspects panel labels, crop coordinates, or bbox metadata. That means the current atlas cannot reproducibly choose the smallest original-paper crop that actually shows what enters the model and the model-facing interface. Policy: prefer cited figure -> cited panel/subpanel -> smallest enclosing crop; if no such crop exists, record `no_suitable_figure` rather than forcing a figure.

High: the persisted figure schema in [scripts/build_input_representation_atlas.py](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/scripts/build_input_representation_atlas.py:367) stores only full-image asset, source path, figure index, caption, description, page number, selection score/reasons, and SHA-256. The UI in [docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js:360) renders that asset as `Original paper figure` with no panel, crop, or provenance boundary. For reproducibility, the atlas needs explicit `panel_id`, `crop_bbox`, `crop_hash`, `source_hash`, `shared_crop_group`, and `selection_uncertainty` fields.

High: the model-node card in [docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js:225) shows only one figure thumbnail plus route previews, while the small illustrative input examples live only in the subtype overview in [docs/input-representation-atlas/index.html](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/index.html:91). That does not satisfy the requested model-node design. Each model node should pair a provenance-backed source crop with a clearly labeled explanatory example of the actual model input, and the two should be visually separated as evidence vs example.

Medium: the current heuristic can attach an unsuitable figure when the route evidence is table-only or otherwise non-figural. Example: `Gemma-7B (LoRA)` has `supporting_figure_or_table: "Table 1"` in [docs/input-representation-atlas/data/atlas.json](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/data/atlas.json:12221), yet the atlas selects `Extended Data Fig. 1` because the caption contains generic scorer/workflow terms. That is a provenance mismatch, not a minimal input crop. The policy should allow `text_only` or `no_suitable_figure` outcomes and never promote a generic overview figure as evidence when the route is not actually figural.

Medium: uncertainty is present in the grounded routes data, but the evidence view does not surface it. See the route-level `uncertainty` field in [docs/input-representation-atlas/data/atlas.json](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/data/atlas.json:9363), and note that the evidence table/detail rendering in [docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js:282) omits it. The policy should explicitly distinguish `evidence-backed`, `shared`, `inferred`, and `uncertain` crops/routes so unsupported edges are not presented as settled ground truth.
recommended_graph: Paper/study node -> original figure node -> panel/subpanel node -> crop node -> route node -> model node.
Separate explanatory example node attached to the model node with `illustrates` or `exemplifies`, never merged into the evidence crop.
risks: Shared figures can collapse distinct model variants into one visual unless the atlas records a `shared_crop_group` and per-model justification for reuse.
Without bbox- and panel-level provenance, the same selected figure asset may not reproduce the same evidence crop on regeneration.
Generic workflow figures can outrank the actual input/interface evidence under the current heuristic, especially when the route support is textual or tabular rather than figural.
acceptance_checks: Every model node has exactly one evidence crop or an explicit `no_suitable_figure` flag, and every crop records `figure_label`, `panel_id(s)`, `page_no`, and `crop_bbox`.
For a random sample of multi-panel papers, the crop is the smallest contiguous region that contains the route evidence and the model-facing interface, with no unnecessary panels included.
For table-only or text-only routes, the atlas does not invent a figure; it surfaces the route as `text_only` or `no_suitable_figure` with uncertainty preserved.
If a figure is shared by multiple model nodes, the UI shows the reuse as intentional and names the shared crop group and per-model rationale.
The model node view renders the provenance-backed crop and the explanatory input example as two separate labeled blocks, and reviewers can tell which one is evidence and which one is illustrative.
